descriptorDirection: higher accessible area / pore volume and moderate CO2 affinity are preferred
whyTheseDescriptorsMatter: The first bottleneck is local reactant availability; accessible pores and CO2 affinity proxies raise the chance that C1 species reach active pockets.

descriptorDirection: moderate-high Lewis acidity and accessible polarized sites are preferred
whyTheseDescriptorsMatter: CO2 activation requires local polarization; the host can provide stable Lewis-acid pockets while a guest metal can add electronic modulation.

descriptorDirection: balanced HCOO* stabilization without strong product trapping is preferred
whyTheseDescriptorsMatter: HCOO* stabilization is the target C1 intermediate step; Mo-type guest motifs can compensate for Al-MOF host activity limitations.
missingDescriptors: direct HCOO* adsorption energy on Al-MOF + Mo

descriptorDirection: hydrated polar pockets and electronically active guest sites are preferred
whyTheseDescriptorsMatter: The route needs local proton transfer and charge redistribution, which is expected to be stronger in a host-guest system than in pristine Al-MOF.

descriptorDirection: moderate product binding and open diffusion paths are preferred
whyTheseDescriptorsMatter: A route that binds HCOO* too strongly may fail at product release; host pore geometry is therefore part of the score.

descriptorDirection: higher C1 selectivity proxy and lower side-reaction risk are preferred
whyTheseDescriptorsMatter: The target route must reduce leakage to C2 organic acids and solid byproducts, especially under hot aqueous conditions.
missingDescriptors: same-condition product distribution for each host-guest route

descriptorDirection: strong hydrothermal scaffold and low leaching risk are required
whyTheseDescriptorsMatter: No activity route is useful if the host collapses or the guest metal leaches before validation.
missingDescriptors: post-reaction 170C PXRD / ICP for Al-MOF + Mo
